findings.reason: the author should home the constant where both crew callers already live (a crew module both import) or state in §18 why the core layer must know a run concept, since the current placement contradicts the "nothing in the core layer imports the crew layer" rule the section invokes.
findings.text: §18 relocates `c-run-` and its predicate from the crew owners `reckon/crew/promotion.py:7209` (`_LANDING_COMMENT_PREFIX`) and `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:123` (`RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX`) into the core module on the sole rationale "beside the card recogniser §17 homes there", which makes core carry crew vocabulary

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 moves the span parser's ~13 helpers and the card recogniser into `reckon/_plan_html.py` behind two public readers (`plan_headings` and the machinery-element predicate) while the parser stays private, and §16 removes the second document walk (`_AuthoredProseParser`) so one parser hides span, identity, extent and prose behind that interface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 hoists the crew landing-comment vocabulary `c-run-` out of `reckon/crew/promotion.py:7209` and `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:123` into the core `reckon/_plan_html.py`, so the core plan-HTML layer owns a crew run-lifecycle constant, inverting the layering rule §18 itself states.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — cited counts public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §17 names its net +2 (retiring `landed_section_ids` as a move and the private walks), §18 names +1 (the run-comment predicate, with the constant a move), and §16 states why nothing is retired, so every section accounts for the surface it adds.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design cites the machinery it extends and every named symbol resolves there, `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` (reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94), the AST census `read_trees`/`definitions` (reckon/interface_counts.py:441,74), `_fingerprint_forms` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:598), `roadmap.implementable_sections` (reckon/roadmap.py:106), and the two soup heading walks the consolidation must converge (`reckon/_store.py:1750`, `:1776`) are all covered by §17's "every heading walk in the package is rewritten" rule rather than left unsearched.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — each proposed layer is justified against extension: §16 states the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over the review reader (it joins `roadmap.implementable_sections` to the union of stored `section_digests` and adds no walk), and §17 keeps `structured_section_spans` as a distinct spans-only contract rather than a second reader over the parser.
